questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I was most motivated to go on exchange to speak more french and to live abroad for a semester.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was a very unique opportunity to study translation between french (which I study) and danish (my first language) in a country with native french speakers.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very good experience. I really enjoyed being abroad, it is so worth all the troubles and confusions in the beginning. People were so helpful and I felt so welcome at the university. Because it is a small city I quickly felt at home. The classes I took also didn't have many people in them so we quickly felt close and got to now each other and the professors.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I got a lot of emails upon arrival, that explained what I had to do

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some of the teachers were very helpful and helped me and my friend find our way, choose the right subjects and assist us in getting settled.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The university had different student accommodations that you could choose from and apply to

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in the student accommodation Cité de la grande Triperie, and there I shared a kitchen with the other students at my floor. We were 16 students per floor. The kitchen was big, but often not that clean. There are individual refrigerators in the rooms. In the accommodation Cité Houzeau and on campus there were cafeterias. The food was affordable and not bad at all!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The housing called Cité Houzeau has a student bar in the basement where there often are parties that can be very loud.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In la grande Triperie, the kitchen was often very un-clean, and sometimes the sink was so clogged that it was impossible to use. The water in the shower changed temperatures between extemely hot and cold, so it was a bit difficult. But overall, it is a nice place to live. There is a lot of storage room in the rooms, that you dont see clearly in the photos available on the website and the room had a lot of light. The rent was rather cheap and the building has a very good placement in the city. You can walk everywhere.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All you need to know is sent by e-mail, and the staff is very helpfull.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was an online registration process where I could donwload my certificate, read about the rules and upload a picture to get my student badge. Then there was a welcome day with a lot of introducing information. I also had to make an appointment at the immigration office and get a permit, which was not complicated at all - but the proces is very analogue:)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A lot of intro meetings were you could ask questions, and they were very helpfull if you called or e-mailed with general questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I had some help from the teachers that could recommend which classes to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Know that they are not super strict about deadlines, you dont have to stress about not knowing the entire proces beforehand. They are super helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the translation courses that I took. It was so special, as a danish person, to be in classes with french speaking people studying danish. We had some really interesting discussions about translating, both into french and into danish. We could really help each other and it felt very much like an "exchange" of languages.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had a translation class with a course on third year of BA and two translation classes with year 1 of MA and then a class of french as a second language only for exchange students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was very different. I studied part time, so I only had 15 ECTS. But I had approximately 10 hours of class, which is almost the same amount of hours as 30 ECTS in Copenhagen. On the other hand, there was not the same amount of preparation and homework. 
In the translation classes the style of teaching was very practical and not so theoretical. 
In the FLE (français langue étrangère/french as a second language) it was very mixed. But the teacher I had was often a bit confusing to follow. It was not very structured in general.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
UT-BM-TRAINT-031-M: Scandinavian Languages Translation (part 1) – 3 ECTS
UT-B3-TRAINT-105-M: Translation and Introduction to Interpretation: Danish – 4 ECTS
UT-BM-TRAINT-045-M: Translation into French: Scandinavian Languages – 2 ECTS
UT-BM-TRAINT-102-M: FLE (French as a second language) – 6 ECTS

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would really recommend the translation courses I had. We were quite few students, so there was more time to go into depth with what we thought was interesting, and the teachers were so nice and very committed.
On the other hand, I can really not recommend FLE (French as a second language) - it was weird and I didn't really get anything from it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It is pretty much the same as in Denmark

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Soap and houshold articles were a bit more expensive, food maybe a bit less expensive. The beer was very cheap:)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I only tried the pilates class once, but it was just me and one other - and a very tired teacher.
But I heard from some of the other students that the volleyball teams were very fun

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was a lot of different sports. There was also "conversation tables" were you could practice speaking french. 
There is also a choir called la Chœur du Pôle hainuyer. I took part in this choir - and it was a highlight of my week

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend the choir la Chœur du Pôle hainuyer. I joined it at the beginning of the semester. There wasn't an admission test, but the level of the singers were quite high, because a lot of them studied at the conservatory. But it is open for all who study or work in the Hainaut district. It is free and it was very fun, and an excellent way of meeting people and practicing pronouncing french words:)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The other small towns nearby, Bruxelles or even a day trip to Paris. When I was in Mons from september to january, I got to see both the mobile "amusement park", the christmas market and the light festival - all in the big square in the city. There are also a lot of places to drink beer and hang out all over the town.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I was on exhange with a friend from Copenhagen, and it made it easier. Overall I did not find it that different from Denmark. In the beginning I was very preoccupied with getting settled and fixing all sorts of paperwork, that I didn't think too much about adjusting to the culture. I felt very much at home. It is a small town, where you quickly get a local feeling. I felt that the people are much more talkative and open than in Copenhagen, which I had to get used to, but ended up really enjoying.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Studying together, eating lunch together. Participating in the erasmus activities or parties. Talk with the students/people you live with. If you live in a university accomodation, you could eat your dinner in the kitchen and then meet the people you live with. Go out in the city and hang out in the bars or cafés.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People seem more social than in Denmark, but this I learned to enjoy:)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Speaking the language. And also the more relaxed approach to paperwork and exams.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Dont stress too much about deadlines and the confusion at first - it gets easier. 
All of the trouble of getting everything in order to go on exchange is so worth it when you get there.
Remember that there is no right way of going on exchange. You dont have to get perfect grades or even feel that you learn that much - living abroad, making new friends and meeting a new culture is also important parts of going.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The feeling of speaking french more freely than when I first got there. And also feeling proud for having completed a semester abroad

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The dirty kitchen were I lived. 
The FLE course. The way of teaching was not my cup of tea.
And not spending all my money in the second hand shops:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
